searchText: how about adding a decaying multiplier to whistleblower and whistleblowing inclusion rewards, something like `1 / inclusion delay`? (inspired by attestation rewards) if you're offline for say 10 minutes or so, and come back online, would your validator still try to send the attestations it was scheduled for during the time you lost your connection? if so, would you get rewarded for it, albeit with a smaller reward due to the higher inclusion distance? **vbuterin** Here's the doc that I promised in the call: **vbuterin** https://hackmd.io/@HWeNw8hNRimMm2m2GH56Cw/HkTzLKOov I'm very surprised by the speed this field moves. The paper on Kate polynomials is only 10 years old, and this proposal is to adopt it massively in the coming years. I had guessed (incorrectly I suppose) that it takes much longer to consider such a scheme to be safe for production **vbuterin** We're already using BLS-12-381 so if the primitives are broken we're already screwed **vbuterin** If you assume that BLS-12-381 works then it's relatively easy to prove the soundness/completeness of Kate-based protocols on top **vbuterin** But yes, BLS itself is definitely relatively close to the bleeding edge of math Elliptic curves cryptography has been around for a while so I suppose that's been tested, the particular curve we're using is not that old but well, I guess some invariants are enough to qualify it as safe. I think the real reason I'm etchy is that I just don't understand what does it mean to "prove soundness" of these protocols. They are probably too far away from my own field to understand that. **vbuterin** In the Kate case the definition of soundness is very easy: you can't make a commitment for a polynomial P "behave like" a commitment for any polynomial other than P **vbuterin** You can state it more formally of course but it's a hash-like one to one mapping property, plus that openings work as expected **vbuterin** Pairings (which Kate uses) are definitely newer than ECC in general! I didn't read much on pairings, just your post on them, but it looked to me as if the definition is just a character of a product of two elliptic curves. So it looks to me as going from a curve to an Abelian surface, if anything should increase security. **vbuterin** My main nagging concern with pairings is something like "if you can do *that* with elliptic curves, what else can you do that we don't even know of?" Perhaps I'm boycotting this channel and burying deeper in the conversation the important document you posted, but promise is the last question regarding pairings. Do you know if you can replace a product of curves in the definition of pairing by an arbitrary Abelian surface with a non degenerate character? There are many more surfaces than products and you can find arbitrarily large groups of rational points. **vbuterin** That I do not know; I am not an expert at this kind of abstract group theory 😢 I know that poeple are probably aware of this, but just wanted to say that the mainnet attestation aggregation is being _ludicrously_ effective. Obviously helped by the high participation, but even then number of blocks that come through with <10 attestations is impressive. Seemls like the launchpad´s timeline and milestones isnt updated yet Any clue why some blocks do not contain any attestations? Maybe it is a bug in one of the clients? Example https://beaconcha.in/block/30998 Very interesting! Either a bug in a client, a very poorly connected node, a node that has an empty mempool from some sort of hard restart right before proposal, or... any number of things. If there are more than a few, I'd suspect a bug The proposer is doing pretty poorly, so I'd guess either he/she is very low on resources/peers or the clock is a little off. The former seems reasonable
